newsitem.title: CHINA: China paper denounces virtual pets as unhealthy.
newsitem.headline: China paper denounces virtual pets as unhealthy.

text.p: Virtual pets, the egg-shaped tamagotchi, are sweeping China but are harmful to children, distracting them from school and family, the official People's Daily said on Monday.

The virtual pet toys shift children's attention from their schoolwork and hamper the development of relationships with their family and classmates, said the newspaper, mouthpiece of the ruling Communist Party.

"Follow-the-crowd consumerism is particularly alarming in a country like ours where conformity is strong," it quoted Wang Zhenyu, a scholar from the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, as saying. Pursuit of fashion was harmful for the development of a child's character, he said.
A manager of a major Beijing department store reported selling 50,000 tamagotchi since first offering them for sale last April, the newspaper said.
The virtual pet toys have a small screen showing a pet that has to be fed, cleaned and put to sleep. It can die of neglect.
Tamagotchi are already banned in schools in Taiwan and Hong Kong.
